Subject: Re: POC packaging — question on surge SKU vs extension

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. The team is aligned on Redwood performance, but procurement pushed back on the pilot packaging options. Two specific asks:

1) Can we get a short SKU-based surge buffer (a small pre-bought pack of burst tokens) instead of extending the timebox? They prefer defined SKU entitlements they can map to our internal budget buckets.

2) If we do the SKU route, procurement wants a nominal credit or price break for the pilot period — they call it a trial-concession to offset integration work.

We want to avoid a long review loop. Would a hybrid — a 2-week extension + a small burst SKU at a modest discount — be something Redwood can support?

Attaching a short SOW draft procurement asked for (POC-SOW-v1.pdf).

Best,
Oliver

Subject: Re: POC packaging — question on surge SKU vs extension

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can do a hybrid. Longer answer — two ways we typically structure this when customers want budget-aligned SKUs and some runway: 

- SKU-first: Provide a small burst pack (e.g., 250k token burst) at pilot rates with an automatic 20% credit applied to any unused portion converted into a post-POC discount if you convert to a committed package within 30 days.

- Timebox-first (extension): Add a 14-day extension to the existing time-box, no SKU, at a reduced daily rate. This avoids SKU accounting but gives calendar runway.

Between the two, the hybrid you suggest is common: 14-day extension + a smaller SKU burst (100k tokens) for peak tests. That buys your engineers time while keeping procurement's SKU visibility.

I'll loop Kimberly (pricing) to confirm the numbers and Marissa on the SOW updates. If procurement wants specific invoice language (line-item SKU names) we can include that in the addendum.

Options I can get approved quickly if you want to move this week:
- Hybrid Offer A: 14-day extension + 100k burst SKU at 15% pilot discount.
- Hybrid Offer B: No extension + 250k burst SKU at 10% pilot discount + conversion credit equal to 20% of unused tokens.

Which framing maps to procurement's preference?

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Oliver / team —

Quick pricing note from legal/finance side for transparency: we can approve Offer A for this pilot under our standard pilot concession rules (max discount 20%, limited to one-time pilot SKU). For Offer B the conversion-credit logic needs a short clause about how unused tokens are reconciled and whether credit converts to committed dollars or future discounts — we usually tie it to an initial 3-month commitment to avoid open-ended credits.

If procurement prefers invoice line items, we can label the SKU "POC-BURST-100K" and include a short usage-runbook line so your finance team can code it properly.

I'm happy to join a 15-minute call with procurement to sign off language.

—Kimberly
Head of Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

[internal note: pricing team ok with 15% on 100k SKU; require conversion window of 30 days for conversion-credit to apply]

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC packaging — question on surge SKU vs extension

Hi Kimberly / Karthik —

Procurement preference is for SKU-first billing (clear ledger mapping). They asked for two clarifications before we sign:

1) Can Redwood commit to a firm expiration on the credit conversion (we prefer 60 days post-pilot rather than 30)?
2) If unused tokens convert to credit, can that credit be applied toward the first-month invoice of any committed plan (not just a 3-month minimum)?

If we can get (1) a 60-day conversion window and (2) credit applicable to first invoice for a confirmed committed plan, procurement will accept the POC-BURST-100K with a 15% pilot discount.

Thanks —
Procurement Team
Oceantide Health

Oliver / procurement —

Good news: finance/legal greenlit a one-off concession to meet your asks with the following binding addendum language we can include in the SOW / invoice: 

- SKU: POC-BURST-100K (100,000 token burst) at 15% pilot discount.
- Expiration: Any unused tokens will be eligible for a credit conversion window of 60 days post-pilot.
- Credit usage: Converted credit may be applied to the first invoice of any subsequent committed plan executed within 60 days of conversion.
- Conversion mechanics: Unused tokens will be reconciled at pilot close; an accounting line and credit memo will be issued.

We will add the above to the POC-SOW and produce an invoice line item for POC-BURST-100K so your ledger can map it. Marissa will update the SOW and circulate the DocuSign link. Once you sign, we can provision the burst pack and enable the 14-day monitoring window we discussed.

Marissa — please push the updated SOW and DocuSign link to this thread.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting the engineer team unblocked.

Karthik
